entry.name: Using Critical Injuries and Death Saves

pages.name: Quick Start
pages.content:
Critical Injuries and Death Saves

The system can automatically create a Critical Injury when damage remaining after cover and armor equals or exceeds a Weapon's Critical rating. The injury is rolled from the table for the final hit location and added to the target Actor.

GM Quick Start

  1. Open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings.
  2. Leave Automate Critical Injuries enabled.
  3. Use the bundled location tables, or replace any table UUID with a world RollTable whose results link to Injury Items.
  4. Set each Weapon's Critical rating correctly.
  5. Apply attack damage from its chat card as normal.

When a lethal injury reaches its deadline, the system posts a Death Save prompt and also shows a die button beside the injury on the Actor's Combat tab.

pages.name: When a Critical Injury Occurs
pages.content:
Trigger and Severity

Protection is resolved before the critical check. A hit causes a Critical Injury only when its final damage is at least the Weapon's Critical rating. Health remaining does not change this test.

Severity Dice

  • Damage equal to Critical, or Critical +1: roll 1D10.
  • Damage at Critical +2 or +3: roll 2D10 and keep the highest.
  • Damage at Critical +4 or +5: roll 3D10 and keep the highest.
  • Continue adding one die for every further two damage.

The linked Injury Item is copied into the target Actor. Its healing formula is rolled once and the number of healing days is stored on that copy.

Immediate Effects

Location-table effects are applied immediately. Arm injuries make the target drop held equipment and may prevent two-handed weapon use. Leg injuries make the target prone and may prevent running. Immobilizing injuries block movement. Instant-death results mark the Actor dead immediately.

pages.name: Incapacitation
pages.content:
Incapacitation

An Actor at zero Health is incapacitated by damage. An Actor at zero Stress Capacity is incapacitated by stress. The Combat tab displays the current state and the token receives a matching status effect.

Damage Incapacitation

The Actor cannot make ordinary Skill rolls or take normal actions. Crawling remains available and is resolved automatically without a Mobility roll.

Stress Incapacitation

The Actor cannot make ordinary Skill rolls. They may Run or seek cover, and those permitted movements are resolved automatically without a Skill roll.

Dead Actors

A dead Actor cannot take actions or make rolls. A GM can still edit the Actor or remove the status manually when correcting world state.

First Aid remains the workflow for restoring Health to an Actor at zero Health. Stabilization is separate: it changes the deadline of a lethal injury but does not restore Health.

pages.name: Lethal Injuries and Death Saves
pages.content:
Lethal Injuries

A lethal Injury Item carries a time limit of Round, Stretch, or Shift.

  • Round: the save becomes due on the patient's next turn in active combat. Outside combat it uses a short world-time deadline.
  • Stretch: the deadline is ten minutes of world time.
  • Shift: the deadline is six hours of world time.

The GM should advance Foundry world time for stretch and shift deadlines. When a deadline passes, the system posts a prompt.

Making the Save

Click Roll Death Save in chat or the die icon beside the injury. The save uses the world-configured Death Save Skill, with Stamina as its default. It costs no action.

  • An Actor who is not incapacitated may push once.
  • An incapacitated Actor may still make the save but cannot push it.
  • Success reschedules the same deadline.
  • Failure marks the Actor dead.

After all allowed pushes, click Apply Result on the roll card.

pages.name: Stabilization
pages.content:
Stabilizing a Lethal Injury

On the patient's Combat tab, click the medical-kit button beside an unstable lethal injury and choose the healer. The roll uses the world-configured Stabilize Critical Injury Skill, with Medical Aid as its default.

Time and Actions

  • A Round-stage injury takes a Slow Action when the healer is in active combat, then rolls immediately.
  • A Stretch- or Shift-stage injury starts timed treatment. Advance world time until the treatment is ready, then click the notes-medical button to resolve it.
  • A conscious patient may treat themselves at −2.
  • An incapacitated patient cannot treat themselves.

Results

  • Success advances Round to Stretch, Stretch to Shift, or Shift to Stabilized.
  • A stabilized injury requires no more Death Saves.
  • Failure locks out another stabilization attempt until the patient has made another Death Save.

After all desired pushes, click Apply Result on the roll card. Stabilization does not heal Health and does not remove the Injury Item.

pages.name: Moving the Wounded
pages.content:
Movement with a Lethal Injury

The Patient Moves

When an Actor with an unstable lethal injury performs a movement action, the completed action card asks for its critical result to be applied. Applying it starts an immediate Death Save. Automatic incapacitated movement follows the same rule.

Someone Else Moves the Patient

  1. Target the patient.
  2. Open Take Action and choose Move wounded character.
  3. Make the configured Medical Aid check. This check itself costs no action; the GM handles the carrier's actual movement normally.
  4. After pushing or accepting, click Apply Result.

On success the patient is moved without an extra save. On failure the patient must immediately make a Death Save.

pages.name: Killing Blows
pages.content:
Killing Blow

A killing blow can target only an incapacitated Character or NPC.

  1. Target the incapacitated Actor.
  2. Choose Killing blow from Take Action.
  3. Spend the Slow Action and make the base Empathy test.
  4. After pushing or accepting, click Apply Result.
  • Success: the attacker cannot carry out the killing blow.
  • Failure: the target is marked dead and the attacker suffers one Stress.

Specialty Bypass

The GM may enter a Specialty Item UUID or exact Item name in the Killing Blow Specialty world setting. An Actor who owns that Specialty bypasses the Empathy test, although the Slow Action is still spent.

pages.name: Configuration and Troubleshooting
pages.content:
Configuration

Action Skills

Open the Action Skills system menu to select world-specific Skill Items for Death save, Stabilize critical injury, and Move wounded character. This keeps the automation usable in worlds with renamed or custom Skills.

Custom Critical Tables

Each location setting accepts a RollTable UUID. Every numbered result must link to an Injury Item. Configure the Injury's location, lethal flag, time limit, healing formula, roll modifiers, and Instant death option as needed.

Troubleshooting

  • No critical appears: confirm automation is enabled, final damage reached Critical, a valid hit location was rolled, and the configured table result links to an Injury Item.
  • A deadline does not advance: start and advance Combat for Round limits, or advance world time for Stretch and Shift limits.
  • No stabilization Skill: configure the action in Action Skills and make sure the healer owns a matching embedded Skill Item.
  • Cannot retry stabilization: a failed attempt intentionally remains locked until the next Death Save.
  • Incorrect state: a GM can edit or delete the Injury Item and can add or remove token statuses manually.
